anglicized_name: Dance platform and temporary shrine building
description_en: There are manydabūs(traditional platforms) in the old settlements of Kathmandu Valley. Most of them were made in the Malla period and were used for the performances of dramas and dances. An inscription found in Nārāyaṇacaura, Naksal from the reign of King Jayadeva the second (713-733 CE) mentions two platforms known asponḍimaṇḍapikāandprekṣaṇamaṇḍapikā(D.VajrācāryaVS 2030, 569 andK. Tamot2013, 20). In the Malla period, many dances and dramas were performed indabūs,especially during festivals and ceremonies (K. Tamot2013, 20).Buṅgamatī's Karuṇāmaya Mandira (BUN0001) collapsed in the devastating earthquakes of 2015. Fortunately, at that time the statue of Buṅgadyaḥ normally enshrined there was on a chariot travelling from Buṅgadyaḥ towards Patan and so remained unharmed. Since the restoration of the temple is likely to last many years, a temporary shrine building has been built on the foundation of thisdabūto house the deity. This shrine building measures 412 × 412 cm and was built using regular brick in mud mortar. It is covered by a roof made of steel trusses, plywood and metal sheets. There were two large stone lions guarding the northern entrance and two smaller lions in front of the southern entrance of the Karuṇāmaya Temple. These have been moved to stand in front of thedabū. A bell suspended from a stone frame was also moved from its original location to the left of the shrine’s entrance.Following the 2015 collapse of the Karuṇāmaya Mandira (BUN0001) this temporary shrine was built to house the main deity of Buṅgadyaḥ (BUN0001-008). Also, two large stone lions (BUN0001-008), two small stone lions (BUN0001-009), and a bell suspended from a stone stand (BUN0001-010) were moved from the temple to the front of this temporary shrine.No sources can be found with which to date the initial construction of thisdabū. Every 12 years, two dances are performed here:jalapyākhã(a dance from Harisiddhi) andgathupyākhã(a dance from Thecho).
description_ne: उपत्यकामा प्राचीन वस्तीका चोक एवं दोबाटोहरूमा दबू (डबली) बनाइएको पाउँछौँ । नृत्य एवं अन्य सांस्कृतिक प्रदर्शनीका निम्ति बनाइएका दबू सतहभन्दा केही भाग माथि उठेको हुन्छ । नृत्य तथा अन्य समारोहका निम्ति लिच्छविकालमा दबू निर्माण भए-नभएको बारे स्पष्ट उल्लेख पाइँदैन । जयदेव द्वितीय (७१३–३३) को नक्साल नारायणचौरको अभिलेखमा पोन्डिमण्डपिका र प्रेक्षण मण्डपीको उल्लेख पाइन्छ (D.Vajrācārya, VS 2030: 569) । यी मण्डपहरू त्यस समयका दबू हुन् भनी तमोटले चर्चा गरेका छन् (K. Tamot2013: 20) । मल्लकालमा धार्मिक नाच एवं नाटकमञ्चनको परम्परा निकै लोकप्रिय बनेको पाइन्छ । यही कालमा उपत्यका र आसपासका नेवार वस्तीभित्र धेरै संख्यामा दबू बने । मल्लकालीन राजदरबारहरूमा पाइने विशेषतामध्ये दबू पनि एक हो । राजपरिवारका कुनै सदस्यको जीवन संस्कार गरिँदा, राजपरिवारबाट कुनै धार्मिक यज्ञ, दान, अनुष्ठानकार्य हुँदा र खास जात्रापर्व (इन्द्रजात्रा, बुङ्गद्यःजात्रा) मनाइने दिन दबूमा नाच नचाउने परम्परा मल्लकालमा प्रचलित थियो (K. Tamot2013, 20) । बुङ्गमती, मच्छिन्द्रबहालको ठुलो चोकको दक्षिण पूर्वी कुनामा यो दबू बनेको छ । दबू निर्माणमिति निर्क्यौल गर्न सकिने कुनै अभिलेख पाइँदैन । हरिसिद्धिमा वार्षिक रूपमा नचाइने हरिसिद्धि नाच १२ वर्षमा एकपल्ट यहाँ नचाउने परम्परा छ । त्यसैगरी ठेचोको गथुप्याखं पनि १२ वर्षमा एकपल्ट नचाइन्छ । यी परम्परागत प्रयोजन अलावा विविध सामाजिक, सांस्कृतिक, एवं राजनैतिक कार्यक्रमको निम्ति यस दबूको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ ।सन् २०१५को भूकम्पमा बुङ्गमतीको करुणामय मन्दिर (BUN0001) भत्किएको थियो । ज्यावलाखेलमा भोटोजात्रा सम्पन्न भए लगत्तै बुङ्गद्यःको मूर्ति करुणामय मन्दिरमा लाने परम्परा छ । भूकम्पले भत्किएको मन्दिर पुनःनिर्माण भैनसकेकाले यसै दबूमाथि अस्थाइ देवस्थल बनाई बुङ्गद्यःको मूर्ति राखिएको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Construction of the temporary shrine of Buṅgadyaḥ
historical_events.event_description: The collapse of Karuṇāmaya Mandira (BUN0001) in the devastating earthquakes of 2015 left Buṅgadyaḥ without a home. Thesaṅghaof 31pānejusof Bungmati built this shrine on the dance platform to temporarely house the deity. Four stone lions and a bell were also moved to this temporary shrine.
